What a route would need and does not have: per-item wording keyed to VR./LN. codes. The ICAR stats pages publish per-item statistics, so route 1 would be available IF the item pool were ever obtained -- record that as the retry plan. route: per-item n fingerprint (re-run of the processing script's filter against the source deposit) + route 6 keying polarity
evidence: data/machivallianism_test.R pivots the deposit's TIPI1..TIPI10 columns by name and drops resp == 0, so each live item's row count is predicted exactly by the non-zero count in the deposit column of that name. route: code_derivation_audit (data/neurlps_2020.R + irw_table_sets per-item n; no route to any item text exists)
evidence: No item_text was shipped, so there is no item<->text mapping to verify: Eedi publishes no question wording as text (arXiv:2007.12061 sec 2.2), and the 948 task-3/4 question images are barred from reuse. What was checked instead is the code derivation. data/neurlps_2020.R sets item = question_id + 1 over an rbind of the task-1/2 AND task-3/4 files, which the guide (p.8) forbids linking because the two ID spaces are anonymized independently. Live aggregates confirm the merge: 27,613 distinct items contiguous 1..27613, not 27,613 + 948 = 28,561; items 1-948 median n = 2,515 vs 396 for items 949-27,613 (6.35x, ~1.89M excess rows, against train_task_3_4.csv's 1,382,727 answers over 948 questions). Codes 1-948 each pool two different questions. Resp axis is likewise broken: the script renames AnswerValue (1-4 option choice) to IsCorrect for the task-2 test files, giving resp = {0,1,2,3,4} with all five levels present on 22,468 of 27,613 items. This establishes that the codes are ambiguous; it establishes nothing about any item's text, because none exists. Computed via irw_table_sets() server-side; the 24,076,951-row table was never fetched.

route: item-code derivation re-run against the source file (per-item n, 5730 items) + rival-hypothesis contrast; no text axis to test
evidence: NO ITEM TEXT SHIPPED, so no item_text<->item mapping exists to verify - status is NO_ROUTE on that axis by construction, not for want of a route. Live per-item n (irw_table_sets server-side aggregate, no export) vs count of non-missing IsCorrect rows per QuestionId in checkins_lessons_checkouts_training.csv: 0 of 5730 items mismatch (item 1 = QuestionId 31769, n 50 vs 50; item 2 = 31770, 44 vs 44; item 5730 = 147933, 6 vs 6). This does NOT establish any item wording, and the n-vector is degenerate - only 133 of 5730 items have an n no other item shares, so a swap of two same-n items would go undetected; it rules out wholesale re-orderings only.

route: re-ran the processing script's derivation over the original source file (core model section 3, script-generated integer codes)
evidence: data/vocabulary_iq.R assigns item = row_number() over the pivoted column order, so the claim under test is items 1-45 = VIQT_data.csv columns Q1..Q45 and items 46-75 = columns S1..S30. Re-running that derivation over the public source file (openpsychometrics.org/_rawdata/VIQT_data.zip, 12173 rows) reproduces four per-item fingerprints of the live table exactly, for all 75 items: non-missing n (item 1/Q1 12161 vs 12161; item 27/Q27 6865 vs 6865; item 43/Q43 6220 vs 6220; item 46/S1 12092 vs 12092), number correct (item 1 11956 vs 11956; item 4/Q4 5207 vs 5207; item 43 3271 vs 3271; items 46-75 all 0 vs 0), and - because the live `id` is row_number() over the same raw file - the sum and sum-of-squares of the respondent ids that answered each item (item 1 sum_id 74037299 vs 74037299; item 62/S17 73398319 vs 73398319). 75 of 75 items match on all four, and the 75 fingerprints are mutually distinct, so the match distinguishes every item from every other rather than only reproducing the set. That distinctness is what separates the four supplemental groups (S27/S28 both n=12047, S14/S19 both 12049, S20/S21 both 12051, S7/S8/S17 all 12061) whose resp is uniformly 0 and which n alone leaves tied: their id sums differ (73280877 vs 73303337; 73319155 vs 73301720; 73317990 vs 73341155; 73407532 vs 73389114 vs 73398319). Scope: this settles the item-to-column mapping. The wording itself is a transcription of the dataset's own codebook, and the two section_prompt strings come from the test page's Procedure paragraph and the codebook's one-line description of the supplemental scale rather than from the administered form. Re-runnable as verify_vocabulary_iq.R (VERDICT: PASS).

That derivation is project-generated content and is flagged for a disclosure ruling.
